name: sdg09
title: SDG 9: Industry, innovation and infrastructure (SDG Atlas of Bolivia 2026)
description: The SDG 9 (Industry, innovation and infrastructure) index of the Atlas de los ODS en Bolivia 2026 (SDSN Bolivia) and the 4 indicators behind it, for Bolivia's 343 municipalities and indigenous autonomies (GAIOC), at two points in time: near the 2012 census and near the 2024 census, stored as 2012 and 2024 so that their change can be studied.

sources.title: Andersen, L. E., & Argandoña, F. (2026). Atlas de los ODS en Bolivia 2026: Brechas y tendencias del desarrollo sostenible en las Entidades Territoriales Autónomas, 2012–2024. La Paz: Universidad Privada Boliviana, SDSN Bolivia.

geo:citation: GeoDevelopment Observatory of Bolivia (2026). SDG 9: Industry, innovation and infrastructure, from the Atlas de los ODS en Bolivia 2026 (343 municipalities, ~2012 and ~2024). https://github.com/quarcs-lab/gdo4bolivia/blob/main/docs/datasets/sdg09.md
geo:notes: Both periods are stored at nominal years: 2012 for the Atlas's initial values (~2012) and 2024 for its final values (~2024). Each indicator's actual reference years differ (e.g. 2008 and 2023 for the health survey, three-year averages for volatile indicators) and are given in its description and in `geo:reference_years`.
Load one variable in both periods, e.g. `geo.load("sdg09", variables="index_sdg9", names=True)`, and its change per unit with `geo.change(df, "index_sdg9")`.

The units are the 343 municipalities and indigenous autonomies (GAIOC) of 2025. Four of them were created after the 2012 census (TIOC-Raqaypampa, San Pedro de Macha, TIOC-Jatun Ayllu Yura and TIOC-Territorio Indígena Multiétnico); the Atlas gives them values in both periods.

Aggregating to provinces, departments or Bolivia (`geo.aggregate`, `geo.combine`) averages the municipal values weighted by census population (`weighted_mean:population`; the 2012 census for ~2012 and the 2024 census for ~2024, loaded from the `sdg` dataset through `geo:weights`): e.g. `geo.aggregate(geo.load("sdg09"), to="department", dataset="sdg09")`. These are population-weighted approximations, not the Atlas's own department figures.

fields.name: geo_id
fields.title: Municipality ID
fields.description: GDO-Bolivia municipality geo ID (BO-DD-PP-MM) of the 343-unit municipality map (SDSN Bolivia 2025: municipalities and indigenous autonomies), numbered as in GADM 4.1 plus four units created since; its boundary is in geo/boundaries/. It nests by prefix into the department (BO-DD) and province (BO-DD-PP) IDs; department and province numbers follow GADM order and differ from INE codes.

fields.name: year
fields.title: Period
fields.description: Period of the values in the row: 2012 holds the Atlas's initial values (near the 2012 census) and 2024 its final values (near the 2024 census). Each variable's actual reference years are given in its description and in geo:reference_years.

fields.name: mun_id
fields.title: INE municipality code
fields.description: Official municipality code of the National Statistics Institute (INE), DDPPMM (department, province, municipality) stored as an integer without the leading zero (e.g. 20101 = Nuestra Señora de La Paz), as in the Atlas. The Atlas's rows are linked to geo_id through this code.
fields.geo:source: Atlas de los ODS en Bolivia 2026

fields.name: index_sdg9
fields.title: Industry, innovation and infrastructure index (0-100)
fields.description: SDG 9 (Industry, innovation and infrastructure) index of the Atlas de los ODS en Bolivia 2026, on a 0-100 scale where 100 means the goal's targets are met and 0 the worst situation. Following the global SDG Index of SDSN, each of its 4 indicators is rescaled linearly to 0-100 between a worst and a best value (given in each indicator's description), with the direction set so that higher is always better and values beyond the bounds capped; the index is the simple mean of the available rescaled indicators. Components: Trunk roads crossing the municipality (number); Internet access, fixed or mobile (% of households); Mobile base stations (per 1,000 people); Fixed or mobile telephone (% of households). Initial value (~2012) stored at 2012 and final value (~2024) at 2024; its components refer to different years around each census. Atlas: “Índice ODS9”.
fields.geo:source: Atlas de los ODS en Bolivia 2026

fields.name: sdg9_1_vpc
fields.title: Trunk roads crossing the municipality (number)
fields.description: Number of roads of the national trunk road network (Red Vial Fundamental) that pass through the municipality. Source: Bolivian Road Administration (ABC), road network of 2012 and 2024. Initial value 2012 (stored at 2012) and final value 2024 (stored at 2024). In the SDG 9 index it is rescaled linearly to 0-100 between 0 (worst, 0) and 3 (best, 100), higher is better, values beyond the bounds capped; the Atlas counts the target as met at 2 and major challenges from 0 on. Atlas indicator 09_01_01_01_vpc, “Número de vías fundamentales que atraviesan el municipio” (Andersen & Argandoña 2026).
fields.geo:source: Atlas de los ODS en Bolivia 2026

fields.name: sdg9_8_ci
fields.title: Internet access, fixed or mobile (% of households)
fields.description: Percentage of private dwellings with people present that have fixed or mobile internet. Source: INE tabulations of the INE Population and Housing Censuses of 2012 and 2024. Initial value 2012 (stored at 2012) and final value 2024 (stored at 2024). In the SDG 9 index it is rescaled linearly to 0-100 between 0 (worst, 0) and 100 (best, 100), higher is better, values beyond the bounds capped; the Atlas counts the target as met at 65 and major challenges from 20 on. Atlas indicator 09_08_01_02_ci, “Porcentaje de hogares con acceso a internet fijo o móvil” (Andersen & Argandoña 2026).
fields.geo:source: Atlas de los ODS en Bolivia 2026

fields.name: sdg9_8_drb
fields.title: Mobile base stations (per 1,000 people)
fields.description: Number of mobile-telephony base stations (radio bases) in the municipality per 1,000 inhabitants. Source: Telecommunications and Transport Regulatory Authority (ATT), 2012 and 2024. Initial value 2012 (stored at 2012) and final value 2024 (stored at 2024). In the SDG 9 index it is rescaled linearly to 0-100 between 0 (worst, 0) and 3 (best, 100), higher is better, values beyond the bounds capped; the Atlas counts the target as met at 3 and major challenges from 0.05 on. Atlas indicator 09_08_01_03_drb, “Densidad de radio bases (por 1,000 habitantes)” (Andersen & Argandoña 2026).
fields.geo:source: Atlas de los ODS en Bolivia 2026

fields.name: sdg9_8_tfc
fields.title: Fixed or mobile telephone (% of households)
fields.description: Percentage of private households that have a fixed or mobile telephone. Source: INE tabulations of the INE Population and Housing Censuses of 2012 and 2024. Initial value 2012 (stored at 2012) and final value 2024 (stored at 2024). In the SDG 9 index it is rescaled linearly to 0-100 between 0 (worst, 0) and 100 (best, 100), higher is better, values beyond the bounds capped; the Atlas counts the target as met at 75 and major challenges from 40 on. Atlas indicator 09_08_01_04_tfc, “Porcentaje de hogares con cobertura de telefonía fija o celular” (Andersen & Argandoña 2026).
